items.question: A firm's profit from producing x units is P(x) = −2x² + 120x − 500 (in ₹). What is the maximum profit the firm can earn?
items.explanation: P'(x) = −4x + 120 = 0 gives x = 30. P'' = −4 is negative, so profit is maximum. P(30) = −1,800 + 3,600 − 500 = ₹1,300.

why_not.B: Left out the −500 term when substituting x = 30 (−1,800 + 3,600).
why_not.D: Gave the output level x = 30 instead of the profit value.
why_not.C: Substituted x = 60 (the root of 120x − 2x²), which is not the maximum point.

items.exam_tip: Set first derivative to zero for x, check the second derivative, then put x back into the original function.

items.question: A Pune-based packaged snacks company, selling namkeen in Maharashtra, launches a new range of protein bars and sells them in the same Maharashtra market to its existing customers. Under Ansoff's matrix, this is:
items.explanation: The market is existing (Maharashtra, same customers) but the product is new (protein bars). New product in an existing market is product development under Ansoff's matrix.

why_not.A: Penetration means selling more of the existing product in the existing market; here the product is new.
why_not.C: Market development means existing product in a new market; here the market is unchanged.
why_not.D: Diversification needs both a new product and a new market; the market is the same here.

items.exam_tip: Ask two questions: is the product new? is the market new? Only new product with old market is product development.

items.paper_name: Direct Tax Laws and International Taxation
items.question: Pine Pvt Ltd (public not substantially interested; not a money-lending company) has accumulated profits of ₹6,50,000 on the date of loan. It lends ₹10,00,000 to Mr. Sen, holding 15% voting power. What is the deemed dividend in Mr. Sen's hands?
items.explanation: A loan by a closely held company to a shareholder holding at least 10% voting power is deemed dividend, but only up to accumulated profits. Here the lower of loan ₹10,00,000 and accumulated profits ₹6,50,000 is taxed.

why_not.A: Taxes the full loan; ignores the cap of accumulated profits.
why_not.C: Takes the excess of loan over profits, which is not the deemed dividend.
why_not.D: Thinks 15% holding is not enough; the test is 10% or more of voting power.

items.exam_tip: Deemed dividend = lower of loan and accumulated profits; shareholder needs 10% or more voting power.
items.applicability: Income-tax Act, 1961 as applicable for A.Y. 2026-27
items.reviewer_note: Section 2(22)(e) concept: 10% voting power threshold; verify no change.
check_notes: Writer: Section 2(22)(e) concept: 10% voting power threshold; verify no change.

Checker: The question does not say Mr. Sen is the beneficial owner of the shares, or that they are not shares entitled to a fixed rate of dividend. Section 2(22)(e) requires both, so students must assume them.

Checker: 'Public not substantially interested' is awkward; it should read 'a company in which the public are not substantially interested'. It would also be clearer to say the company 'possesses' accumulated profits.
Second checker: The question doesn't say Mr. Sen is both registered and beneficial owner of the shares. This is implied by "holding 15% voting power".
Second checker: The question doesn't say the loan is not in the ordinary course of business. The statement that it is not a money-lending company covers this.
Second checker: Nothing in the question says whether the accumulated profits include current-year profits up to the date of the loan. The phrase "on the date of loan" covers this.
